title: A front-end extension: WEB_DIRECTORY and registerExtension
hook: One line of Python and one JavaScript file put your code in the editor. Here is what gets served, what gets loaded, and which hook to use.

verified.claim: A pack's WEB_DIRECTORY is added to EXTENSION_WEB_DIRS under the pack's folder name.
The /extensions route lists **/*.js under each folder, and each folder is served as a static path at /extensions/<name>.
A pyproject web setting registers the folder under the project name, not the folder name.
Only .js files are added to the page, other files are reached by URL, and the page's example imports app from ../../scripts/app.js.
The hook order on page load.
A running server here answered GET /extensions with a JSON list of .js paths.
verified.ref: a read-only request on our test machine

unchecked: We did not load an extension in a browser for this lesson. The hook order is what the docs state, and we did not trace it through the shipped front-end bundle.
The arguments each hook receives are from the docs. Apart from the example here, we did not test them.
Whether editing a served .js file needs only a page reload. We expect so, since files are served from disk, and we did not try it.
